recorded_at.head_note: Enumerated at d15e614 and recorded against c94612d, the register's own head, because `git diff c94612d d15e614` over FULL_GLOBS is EMPTY: the mutated files are byte-identical at the two commits, and an identical pinned cargo-mutants over identical bytes enumerates identically. THE SQUASH FOR PUBLICATION replaced this branch's 166 commits with one, so the commit this was recorded at is not in published history and `head` names c8616a9, which is. This is the same reconciliation the census's own note already makes and it is held to the same test: MEASURED, `git diff c94612d c8616a9` over FULL_GLOBS is EMPTY -- the mutated files are byte-identical at the campaign's head and here -- and `git diff 6ab75a4 c8616a9` is empty over the WHOLE tree, because the squash was built from the pre-squash tip's tree object unchanged. So the measurement still describes this tree; what it can no longer do is say WHICH earlier commit it was taken at, and with one commit in the range the drift check has nothing to diff against and is vacuous here. It becomes meaningful again at the next commit that touches FULL_GLOBS. Every other commit reference in this file -- run identifiers, the ratcheted-from head, the campaign named in prose -- is a historical citation that no gate resolves, and is left exactly as written.

what: Every mutant the full-scope campaign at `recorded_at.head` enumerated, keyed as the survivor register is keyed and counted rather than listed. It answers the one question 144 survivor rows cannot: whether a mutant found at some later commit is one this measurement has ever seen. A brand-new function's mutants are in no row and in no count, which is how they stop being invisible.
